title: Efficient and Optimal Learning of Discrete Distributions with Person-Level Privacy
abstract: arXiv:2610.31612v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study learning a discrete distribution under person-level differential privacy in the batched setting. Given $n$ users, each contributing $m$ i.i.d. samples from an unknown distribution $\mu$ over $[k]$, we seek an estimate of $\mu$ with total-variation error $\alpha$. We give polynomial-time algorithms under both pure and approximate differential privacy. Under pure $(\varepsilon,0)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(\alpha^2 m)+k/(\alpha\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k/\varepsilon)$, the first polynomial-time pure-DP guarantee matching the information-theoretic optimum up to logarithmic factors. Under approximate $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP, we achieve $n = \widetilde O(k/(\alpha^2 m)+k/(\alpha\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k+\log(1/\delta)/\varepsilon)$. At $\delta=2^{-\Theta(k)}$, this is $\widetilde O(k)$ for fixed $\alpha,\varepsilon,m$ and failure probability. translated_title: 具有个人级隐私保护的离散分布高效最优学习
translated_abstract: 我们研究了在批处理（batched）设置下，在个人级差分隐私约束下学习离散分布的问题。给定 $n$ 个用户，每个用户贡献 $m$ 个来自 $[k]$ 上未知分布 $\mu$ 的独立同分布样本，我们寻求总变差误差为 $\alpha$ 的 $\mu$ 估计量。我们在纯差分隐私和近似差分隐私下均给出了多项式时间算法。在纯 $(\varepsilon,0)$-DP 下，我们达到了 $n = \widetilde O(k/(\alpha^2 m)+k/(\alpha\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k/\varepsilon)$ 的样本复杂度，这是首个在对数因子内匹配信息论最优界的多项式时间纯 DP 保证。在近似 $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-DP 下，我们达到了 $n = \widetilde O(k/(\alpha^2 m)+k/(\alpha\sqrt{m}\varepsilon)+k+\log(1/\delta)/\varepsilon)$。当 $\delta=2^{-\Theta(k)}$ 时，对于固定的 $\alpha$、$\varepsilon$、$m$ 和失败概率，样本复杂度为 $\widetilde O(k)$。我们的算法采用了一种新的六阶和平方（degree-6 sum-of-squares）估计器，用于从不可信的批（摘要在此处截断）……
tldr: 本文首次在个人级纯差分隐私下实现了批处理设置中学习离散分布的多项式时间算法，其样本复杂度在对数因子内匹配信息论最优界，并在近似差分隐私下同样达到近最优的 $\widetilde O(k)$ 样本复杂度，核心技术贡献是一种新的六阶和平方估计器。
en_tdlr: This paper gives the first polynomial-time pure-DP algorithms for learning discrete distributions in the batched person-level privacy setting that match the information-theoretic optimum up to logarithmic factors, and achieves near-optimal $\widetilde O(k)$ samples under approximate DP, via a novel degree-6 sum-of-squares estimator.
